headline: Anthropic's debut can't save the AI trade: S&P −2.0%, Nasdaq −2.3%, Dow −1,101 points
summary: Stocks opened higher on enthusiasm for Anthropic's record IPO, with the S&P 500 up as much as 1.3%, but the rally collapsed after the stock began trading shortly before noon and AI names reversed hard into the close. The selling was broad: more than 90% of S&P 500 members fell, decliners beat advancers about 4.5-to-1 on the NYSE, only one Dow stock rose, and the S&P 500 logged a sixth straight loss, its longest losing streak since April 2024, leaving it 8.2% below last month's record.
drivers: AI trade reverses after Anthropic's debut

Anthropic opened at $111.50, 34% above its $83 IPO price, briefly topped $115 and closed at $97.17 (+17.1%), but the early AI bounce faded as it traded: Nvidia went from +4.7% to −3.3% at $145.98, Micron from +7.8% to −2.1%, CoreWeave from +10.5% to −6.1%, and the SOX fell 2.4% with 27 of its 30 members lower.
AMD sinks on a short-seller report

AMD fell 7.7% to $489.19 after Hunterbrook disclosed a short and alleged blacklisted Chinese server maker IEIT kept receiving AMD firmware, plus heavy financing commitments to AI customers; Marvell lost 4.9%, while Intel bucked the tape, up 1.9%.
Retail and health care add to the losses

Williams-Sonoma dropped about 15% on a slight revenue miss and an unchanged outlook, Walmart slipped 1% despite a beat and raised guidance, and UnitedHealth fell 5.6% as worries over a proposed Medicare Advantage audit rule kept pressure on insurers.
Softer data trims yields only slightly

Initial jobless claims rose to 203,000 and continuing claims jumped 70,000 to a ten-week high of 1.763 million, while the Philly Fed index slowed to 6.3 from 20.9; the 10-year yield eased about 1bp to 5.05% and the VIX jumped 15.8% to a six-month high. Palo Alto (+6.4%) and CrowdStrike (+2.7%) were rare gainers.
week: Four sessions in, the S&P 500 is down 5.1%, the Nasdaq 5.0%, the Dow 6.2% and the Russell 2000 4.9% for the week, with the 10-year yield still above 5% and a December Fed hike widely expected after hawkish minutes.
watch: Next: reactions to Intuit, Gap and Ross Stores results and the expiry of December WTI on Fri Nov 20, Dell's results on Tue Nov 24, a shortened Thanksgiving week, and the Fed meeting on Dec 8–9.
